scenes.script_line: We say, 'Throw it away.' But where is away? A wrapper dropped beside a worksite can move with the wind, enter a ditch or stay in the soil. It has not disappeared. It has only changed location. On a site where we build for the future, our waste also has a future. Put it in the right place.

wide shot of a ditch beside a building site with loose litter nearby
medium shot of a worker picking up rubbish and placing it in a bin
close-up of hands sorting waste into a labelled bin

scenes.script_line: Imagine spending twenty years building something extraordinary. Every day matters. Every detail counts. Now imagine leaving one plastic bottle behind. Some plastics can persist in the environment for decades or even centuries, slowly fragmenting rather than simply vanishing. One careless minute can leave a trace far beyond a working career. We build to last. Let's not leave pollution to last too.

shots.text: wide shot of a finished garden structure built over many seasons
close-up of a plastic bottle left on the ground among plants
medium shot of a crew member collecting a discarded bottle into a bag
close-up of hands tying off a full rubbish bag

scenes.script_line: A cigarette butt is tiny. But most cigarette filters contain a type of plastic. Left on the ground, they can release contaminants and break into smaller pieces. A lit cigarette can also create a fire risk in dry vegetation. Think of the hours spent preparing one beautiful landscape. Is that worth risking for one butt? Use the approved receptacle, where smoking is permitted.

scenes.script_line: A loose strip of packaging lies beside the materials. 'I'll get it later,' someone thinks. Then the wind arrives. The plastic catches on a bush, or travels toward water. The wind has no bin and no understanding of our intentions. One simple action changes the ending: collect loose waste as you work. Don't leave the cleanup to the weather.

scenes.script_line: Metal, timber, plastic packaging and concrete rubble are not all the same. Some can be reused. Others need separate waste streams and authorised collection. Mixing everything may make recovery harder. The question is not simply, 'Where can I throw this?' It is, 'Where should this material go?' Good construction includes a plan for what remains afterward.
